claims.text: Machine-learning-based inverse design integrating high-throughput computational screening with experimental feedback can rapidly identify RHEA compositions that combine intrinsic strength, ductility, and low weight.
The starting refractory-alloy design space is a broad, multi-principal-element composition space.
The starting composition space has not previously been optimized for mechanical performance.
An inverse-design framework can analyze existing thermo-kinetic data and simulation outputs to predict candidate RHEA compositions.
Suitable databases are available to train the proposed machine-learning model.
Specific refractory-element combinations and concentrations determine microstructural phase stability.
Specific refractory-element combinations and concentrations determine defect distributions.
The machine-learning model can learn relationships among alloy composition, microstructural evolution, and mechanical properties.
Predicting composition-structure-property correlations enables optimization of RHEA compositions for high strength, ductility, and reduced density.
ML-designed alloys will have higher strength than alloys designed solely through traditional thermo-kinetic simulations or empirical methods.
ML-designed alloys will have higher ductility than alloys designed solely through traditional thermo-kinetic simulations or empirical methods.
ML-designed alloys will have lower density than alloys designed solely through traditional thermo-kinetic simulations or empirical methods.
Sparse training data may limit the inverse-design approach.
Extreme elemental segregation or very low mutual solubility may produce unpredictable microstructures and limit the approach.
Model predictions may not remain accurate in unexplored regions of RHEA composition space.
